thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: multiple model-init failures in us-west-2 GPU pool — elevated error rate, paging oncall @priya-nguyen :rotating_light:
priya-nguyen: Ack. I’m on it, moving to #incidents-call. Can someone post the first failing logs?
javier-rte: putting a tail of one init log here:
javier-rte: ```
[2026-04-05T14:05:12Z] model-init: loading weights redwood-rlhf-xl-30b-8bit
[2026-04-05T14:05:14Z] cuda: cuMemAlloc failed: out of memory
[2026-04-05T14:05:14Z] runtime: kernel compile timeout after 60s
[2026-04-05T14:05:15Z] deser: gzip: invalid header
[2026-04-05T14:05:16Z] container: exit status 137
```
emily-sre: seeing node flaps — kube reports OOMKilled then node-marked-not-ready for 2 nodes in pool-gpu-2
sam-support: customer-impact: 12 customers in the last 10m with 502s on /v1/generate, error rate ~18%, latency spike to 3s for fallbacks
priya-nguyen: immediate mitigation: take affected nodes OOS for new loads, route new requests to backup pool us-west-2b and fallback-small-hosted for requests that hit canaries
liu-platform: started routing rule update — traffic migration to us-west-2b in progress (prefers instances with larger GPU memory). ETA ~40s
javier-rte: hypotheses: (1) large model artifact got corrupted during artifact streaming causing deser failures; (2) aggressive JIT compile + low free GPU memory triggers compile timeout and OOM; (3) warmup prefetch is stampinged across nodes
priya-nguyen: plan: 1) disable prefetch/warmup for this model; 2) restart orchestration for failed pods with SKIP_COMPILE=1 and SKIP_PREFETCH=1; 3) enable soft-fallback policy to rwd-small-v1 for any request that can't allocate KV cache in 200ms
emily-sre: I’ll cordon the two flapping nodes and evict pods. Also increasing kube eviction threshold temporarily to avoid repeated churn.
sam-support: drafting status page blurb now — will call it "degraded performance for model serving in us-west-2" and note mitigation steps. Do we notify customers directly?
priya-nguyen: yes - page top affected customers (IDs: cust-9983, cust-1024, cust-4512) — send exec summary: cause unknown, mitigation in flight, possible degraded quality for high-context requests
javier-rte: started a rolling restart with env SKIP_COMPILE=true on the replacement nodes. Command used:
javier-rte: ```bash
kubectl set env deploy/model-server SKIP_COMPILE=true --namespace=prod-us-west-2
# then trigger graceful-redeploy.sh --selector=model=redwood-rlhf-xl-30b-8bit
```
javier-rte: also kicked an artifact verifier against S3 bucket for that model, checking for partial objects / checksum mismatch
liu-platform: artifact verifier returned: one multipart part failed checksum for artifact redwood-rlhf-xl-30b-8bit/weights.tar.gz.part3 — marking as suspect and re-pulling from origin
priya-nguyen: good. while re-pull happens, keep routing to backups and keep warmup off. If restarts succeed, we’ll canary one node with full load at 1% traffic
emily-sre: after cordon+evict, nodes stabilized. New pods coming up on us-west-2b with SKIP_COMPILE env. No more immediate cuda OOM in new logs so far
sam-support: status page updated, and customers notified via support tickets with note about degraded performance and fallback options :white_check_mark:
priya-nguyen: handoff to javier for verification + postmortem. I’m staying on the call until canary completes. Next steps: collect kernel compile logs, artifact checksums, and warmup telemetry.
javier-rte: taking over. I’ll run a targeted rerun of the JIT compile locally to reproduce the timeout and capture nvcc logs. Back here in 20.
incident-bot: INCIDENT: oncall handoff from priya-nguyen to javier-rte at 1751004385
javier-rte: noted. adding follow-ups: (A) create SRE ticket for artifact replication gap, (B) add compile timeout alert at 40s for this model class, (C) add soft-prefetch rate limiter to prevent stampede.
priya-nguyen: thanks team — closing paging once canary at 1% is healthy for 10m. Will open postmortem template after incident closed. :raised_hands:
